claims.subject: MCP surface: `watch` and `init` tools
claims.why: The original asks for a complete MCP surface, but TOOLS exposes only 8 of the 10 CLI commands; a Bot can rent through MCP but cannot start the guard that enforces the cap (docs/mcp.md admits this is a gap)

claims.subject: End-to-end proof of the guard (`watch`) on a real rented GPU
claims.why: The paid M2 runs covered up/run/pull/down/ledger only; the table marks `watch` stopping a live pod as 'only described', so the cap, which is the tool's core promise, was never proven on a real billing machine

claims.subject: guard idle rule (idle_since_start_minutes)
claims.why: `watch` passes the wall-clock minutes since the guard started as `idle_since_start_minutes` whatever the GPU utilisation, and `effective_idle_minutes` takes the max, so with the default 10-minute window a busy machine gets stopped as 'idle' after about 10 minutes of watching; no test covers this, because every test runs with interval=0

claims.subject: `up --json` and MCP `rentguard_start` structured output
claims.why: `_open_if_needed`, `_print_access` and the `wait_running` log call `print()` rather than `note()`, so in --json mode stdout carries prose before the JSON document; this breaks the documented 'exactly one JSON document' contract, and MCP start returns no structuredContent on success

claims.subject: MCP `rentguard_run` command handling
claims.why: `dispatch` splits the command string on whitespace and the CLI then shell-quotes each word, so a compound or quoted command sent through MCP reaches the remote shell mangled; this is the same defect M2 paid to find and fixed only on the CLI path

claims.subject: Documentation of F-4 (--dry-run) and F-5 (idle clamp)
claims.why: The docs (KNOWN-FAILURES, cap.md, limitations.md, quickstart.md, VERIFICATION.md) still say --dry-run rents machines and must not be used, and that the idle clamp is missing with no test, but cli.py checks dry_run before create, guard.py clamps idle to uptime, and tests/test_money_paths.py covers both, so the docs describe a different tool from the code

claims.subject: Documented test evidence (74 tests; test_money_paths = 33)
claims.why: cap.md, VERIFICATION.md, providers.md and fake.md cite 74 tests with 33 in test_money_paths, but the tree has 39 tests in that file plus tests/test_runpod_transport.py, which no doc lists, so the stated evidence no longer matches the suite

claims.subject: Real-rental proof record (count and cost)
claims.why: CHANGELOG, quickstart, VERIFICATION and M2-REAL-RENTAL record two rentals for $0.017, while CHARTER.md R5 claims 3 rentals for $0.0264, and no file in the tree documents the third

claims.subject: Release-readiness definition
claims.why: The status table says nothing remains before the publication ask, yet its own definition of 'publishable' has no check for a complete MCP surface or a proven guard, both of which the original requires

claims.subject: ssh known-hosts handling on non-Windows
claims.why: limitations.md says UserKnownHostsFile=NUL applies on Windows, but RunPod.ssh_argv hardcodes the literal 'NUL' on every OS (the `{null}` placeholder that cli._ssh substitutes is never used), so on Linux/macOS ssh writes a file named NUL

claims.subject: tests/_artefacts/ (assay probe scripts and UTF-16 PowerShell transcripts)
claims.why: Internal audit transcripts, which record failures from old revisions and absolute local paths, are tracked in what is meant to be a publishable release tree, and the original never asked for them

claims.subject: 94% code / 100% feature coverage target attributed to the user
claims.why: coverage.py and ci.yml present '94% of the code with 100% of the features' as the target the user set, but the frozen original contains no coverage target
